input: This summary presents the case for a heat-recovery retrofit at the food plant and sets out the recommendation arising from the analysis. The plant currently uses 2326 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, which represents a significant ongoing operating cost. According to projections provided by the equipment vendor, the proposed retrofit is expected to save 14% of this electricity use, which corresponds to a derived saving of 326 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit is $500k. At an electricity price of $0.09 per kWh, the derived annual saving amounts to $29k, giving a derived simple payback of 17.2 years. It is important to note that the saving figure is a vendor projection and has not been measured at this plant, and furthermore the refrigeration load in the summer peak month has not been modelled, which means that the projection carries a degree of uncertainty. In light of these considerations, it is recommended that a metered trial be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is made. The plant engineer will own the trial, and the results of the trial will inform the subsequent decision-making process.
target: The recommendation is a metered trial of the heat-recovery retrofit on one of the three refrigeration lines, before any capital decision, and the plant engineer owns the trial. The food plant uses 2326 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. The equipment vendor projects that the retrofit saves 14% of that use, a derived saving of 326 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $500k. At an electricity price of $0.09 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $29k and the derived simple payback is 17.2 years. A payback of that length rests on a saving that is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the projection is untested at the plant's highest load. The metered trial replaces the projected saving with a measured saving on one line, on metered use, before the capital is committed. The trial is confined to one line, and its result is the evidence base for the decision on the remaining lines. The trial reports the measured saving against the same electricity price, and the capital decision then rests on a plant figure rather than a vendor figure.
